chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding the words of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him): 'I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be of your own free will,' whichever of the two terms he fulfilled? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fulfillment from these two was the furthest of the two, ten years.' I said: 'So did he go to her before the condition expired, or after its expiration?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Before it expired.'

I said to him: 'So if a man marries a woman and stipulates to her father the wage of two months, is that permissible?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Moses (peace be upon him) knew that he would complete the condition for him, but how can it be for this one that he would know that he would remain (alive) until he fulfills it for him? And indeed, during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a man used to marry a woman on the basis of a Surah from the Quran, or on the basis of a Dirham, or on the basis of a handful of wheat.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stipulating a period of service or a specific amount as a condition in a marriage contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the juristic principle of *Ijarah* (service) as a valid marital consideration, emphasizing that the stipulator's knowledge of the condition's fulfillment validates the contract. It bridges the narrative of Prophet Shu'ayb (AS) with the Prophetic era practice of marrying for minimal, tangible assets like a Quranic chapter or wheat, highlighting the flexibility of *Mahr* in Shia jurisprudence. The Imam’s reasoning underscores that certainty of performance, rather than the nature of the asset, is the key to validity.
